title: Constant-rate binary locally decodable codes with logarithmic query complexity
formal: Do binary codes of constant rate and constant error tolerance exist whose randomized local decoder recovers any requested message bit with O(log n) queries and success probability at least 2/3?
context:

sentences: A locally decodable code recovers one requested message bit by reading only a few positions of a corrupted codeword.
The proposal asks for binary codes with constant rate, constant error tolerance, and O(log n) randomized queries.
Local recovery must work for every message position despite a globally adversarial set of corruptions.
Such codes would combine economical storage with inexpensive access to individual protected bits.
The saved proposal gives a success probability of at least two thirds but does not fully specify the length parameter or explicitness requirements, which remain necessary for a finished formulation.
